clue.text: I've put animal in transit, controlling others in an underhand way

definitions.text: controlling others in an underhand way

indicators.note: things in transit are being moved about, so the letters of the fodder are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone transporting an animal confesses to moving it about, in a scheming tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in transit' sounds like the animal is travelling, but it tells you to rearrange all twelve letters of I'VE PUT ANIMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A manipulative person exerts devious, sly influence over people to get their own way.

clue.text: Communist China's leader's entering trading area

indicators.note: one piece going into another, so the leader's name with its S sits inside the market word

parts.note: a mart is a market, a place for trading
Xi Jinping is China's leader; the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A news item about the Chinese president visiting a market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China's leader' tempts you to take the first letter C, but it means the country's actual leader, Xi Jinping.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Karl Marx's theories is a communist; the two terms are near synonyms.

clue.text: i newspaper printed in New York, which is neat

indicators.note: the paper's letters appear inside, as if printed within the city's abbreviation

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a newspaper

explanation.surface: A British paper called i is being published in New York, which is tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a real British newspaper, which makes the lower-case i look like part of the scene; here it is just the letter I, followed by FT, the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty and neat are both informal words for clever, smart or handy.

clue.text: Lawyer's assistant: average girl, drinks beer

indicators.note: to drink is to take in, so the beer goes inside the other letters

parts.note: par is the average or normal standard
gal is an informal word for a girl
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A legal assistant is described as an ordinary woman who drinks beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A paralegal is a trained worker who helps solicitors or attorneys but is not a qualified lawyer.

clue.text: Live on English sole

parts.note: L marks the live terminal on an electrical plug

explanation.surface: Advice to live on a diet of English sole, the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' tempts you towards the fish, but it means only. L is the live wire on a UK plug, beside N for neutral and E for earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole as an adjective means single or only one, which is what lone means.

clue.text: Drink it when reflecting in the morning air

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: a.m. means in the morning
an aria is an air, a song in opera

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a drink while musing in the fresh morning air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflecting' reads as musing in the surface, but it is a mirror image that reverses the word it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a brand of coffee liqueur, so it is an example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Clergyman obtained second-hand sheds: money promised

indicators.note: to shed is to cast off, so the promises of payment are removed from the longer word

parts.note: vicarious experience is felt second-hand, through someone else
IOUs are written promises to pay money

explanation.surface: A priest buys second-hand garden sheds on a promise of payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheds' looks like a noun, garden huts, but it is a verb: VICARIOUS drops IOUS, IOUs being notes promising money.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest in the Church of England, a kind of clergyman.

clue.text: Son's holiday with an exotic dancer?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a trip is a short holiday
per means for each or with an, as in 'ten pounds per hour'

explanation.surface: A son goes on holiday accompanied by an exotic dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripper performs a striptease, which is a form of erotic dancing; the question mark flags the euphemism.

clue.text: Pick cold snack that's less cold

indicators.note: being less one thing means losing it, so a single letter is taken away

parts.note: a choc ice is a block of ice cream coated in chocolate, a cold treat
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Choose a frozen treat that is not quite so chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: A choc ice is a British ice-cream bar coated in chocolate; remove one C (cold) from CHOCICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A choice is the thing you pick, or the act of selecting from options.

clue.text: Votes, official but incomplete, and blunders

indicators.note: something incomplete is missing its end, so the last letter of the official goes

parts.note: a referee is a match official

indicators.note: a word that blunders goes wrong, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A complaint that the ballot officials botched an incomplete count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts REFEREE to REFERE; 'blunders' scrambles AND into NDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are public ballots on a single question, so they are a kind of vote; the plural matches.

clue.text: Concealed difficulty in contract? Strike

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hidden snag or drawback
second meaning: to hit, as in 'the blow caught him on the chin'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a labour dispute, a strike clause hidden in a contract; the two parts are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a hidden problem in a deal, and to catch someone is to hit them with a blow.

clue.text: Silly, silly duke shown in scenes of happy innocence

indicators.note: silly means foolish or crazy, which suggests the letters of the first word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A foolish aristocrat appears in some pastoral paintings of innocence.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Silly' is the fodder and the second is the anagram signal; SILLY plus D (duke) rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Idylls are picturesque, peaceful episodes or poems depicting carefree rural life.

clue.text: Intellectual welcomes a hard opening to interview for Middle Eastern native

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the letters go inside the intellectual

parts.note: a brain is a clever person
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so take the first letter

parts.note: first letter I

explanation.surface: A clever interviewer greets someone from the Gulf at the start of the meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bahraini is a person from Bahrain, a Gulf island state in the Middle East.

clue.text: Caribbean island also conserves land

indicators.note: to conserve is to keep safe inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: too means also
to bag or land something is to win or catch it

explanation.surface: A Caribbean island also protects its land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in landing a fish or a job: BAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is the smaller island of Trinidad and Tobago in the Caribbean Sea.

clue.text: Turbulent times in which unusual result is accepted

indicators.note: signals that the multiplication word holds something within it
being accepted means being taken in, so the jumbled letters go inside

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in 'three by four'

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In stormy times, an unexpected outcome is tolerated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'times' is not a period but the multiplication sign, read as 'by' in 'two by three'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blustery weather is gusty and wild, so it is turbulent.

clue.text: Student lied, unfortunately, about photographs being returned

indicators.note: around, so the jumbled letters surround the reversed pictures
suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged
returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pics is short for pictures, photographs

explanation.surface: A student lied, sadly, about some photos being sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' in the surface, but here it means around: the scrambled letters wrap the reversed pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower or pupil learning from a teacher, so a student.

clue.text: Boat of Spaniard left to go to ruin

indicators.note: left gives way and ruin takes its place: the letter for left goes and the new word comes in

parts.note: a Catalan is someone from Catalonia in Spain
to mar is to spoil or ruin

explanation.surface: A Spaniard's boat was abandoned to rot.
explanation.walkthrough: In CATALAN, the L (left) is replaced by MAR (ruin).
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a sailing vessel with two parallel hulls.

clue.text: Lake emptied after Italian's head hidden in waterway for The Mob

indicators.note: the emptied lake comes after the rest
a letter concealed within the waterway goes inside it

parts.note: a canal is a man-made waterway

indicators.note: a head is the top or front, so take the first letter

parts.note: first letter I

indicators.note: emptied means the inside is taken out, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: outer letters L and E

explanation.surface: An Italian gangster's corpse is hidden in a drained canal near a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaille is a contemptuous word for the rabble or common people, the mob.

clue.text: Row audibly about pressure in protective helmet

indicators.note: heard rather than seen, so the rowing word is taken for how it sounds

parts.note: to scull is to row a boat
CA (circa) means about

explanation.surface: A noisy quarrel about having to wear a helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests an argument, but it is rowing a boat: SCULL, heard as SKULL.
explanation.definitionFit: A skullcap is a close-fitting cap; in older armour it was a protective metal cap for the head.

clue.text: Poles wish to inform

parts.note: S and N stand for the south and north poles, the two poles of the Earth or a magnet
an itch is a craving or wish

explanation.surface: Polish people want to pass information to the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' is not people from Poland but the two poles, S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To snitch is slang for telling tales or informing on someone.

clue.text: Set in motion metal hoop right away

indicators.note: sent away means removed, so the letter for right is dropped

parts.note: a stirrup is the metal loop for a rider's foot

explanation.surface: Someone gets a stirrup moving by pushing it to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up trouble or action is to provoke it, to get it started.

clue.text: Examination of country's aluminium

parts.note: Peru is a South American country; the 's adds S
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: An inspection of a South American nation's aluminium output.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or inspection of something.

clue.text: Harry beating Henry guaranteed

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, which suggests the letters are disturbed and reordered

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Prince Harry beating Prince Henry is a certainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name, a prince alongside Henry, but is the verb meaning harass, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the bag is idiomatically secured or certain, as good as won.

clue.text: Again end up getting duck

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to die is to come to an end

explanation.surface: Someone dies again after being given a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RE and DIE together in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck, famous for its soft down.

clue.text: Hinder international couple stashing away millions

indicators.note: to stash is to hide something inside, so the millions go within the other letters

parts.note: a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A jet-setting couple hiding their fortune blocks an investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to damage or weaken it, so to hamper or obstruct it.

clue.text: Are nurses beginning to despair over love?

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the word Are holds the other letters
the beginning is the first letter

parts.note: first letter D
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over, a set of six balls

explanation.surface: A question whether nurses start to despair of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like the medical staff, but it is the verb meaning hold close: the word Are cradles the other letters. O for over is a cricket scorebook convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore someone is to love them deeply; both are verbs.

clue.text: Fruit is repulsive when picked up

indicators.note: picking up a word is hearing it, so the answer sounds like the word for repulsive

parts.note: ugly means repulsive

explanation.surface: A fruit that looks repulsive when you lift it.
explanation.walkthrough: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit with knobbly, unattractive skin, pronounced like ugly.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugli is a citrus hybrid of grapefruit and tangerine, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Swore last of patients would leave disease-free

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter is removed

parts.note: cursed means swore

indicators.note: the last of a group is its final member, so only the closing letter of the word is used

parts.note: last letter S

explanation.surface: A doctor swore that the last patients would walk out healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient who has been cured has recovered and is healthy again.

clue.text: See royal knocked back slightly diluted alcoholic drinks

indicators.note: to knock back is to push in reverse, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to spot is to see
regal means royal

explanation.surface: Watching a royal down some weak drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' suggests drinking, but it reverses the whole run. A lager top is lager with a dash of lemonade on top, a British pub order.
explanation.definitionFit: A lager top is beer with a little lemonade added, making it weaker than straight lager.

clue.text: Source of free-flowing water, primarily less saline

definitions.text: Source of free-flowing water, primarily less saline

indicators.note: flowing freely means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: water and saline are taken as written, with L between them because primarily means firstly, picking the opening letter of less

explanation.surface: A spring of water that flows unaided is, in the main, less salty.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of WATER, L (first of less) and SALINE are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well taps groundwater under pressure, so it rises naturally without pumping; such fresh groundwater is generally not briny.
